text: In this story, a house floats on water. Where is the house?
The house is on the water.
Before, the house floated on water. Now move it to dry ground. Correct the old claim.
The house is not on the water.
Look at the story picture card. Find and fix one word about the place.
The house is on land.
In this story, a house floats on water. Where is the house?
The house is on the water.
The house stands on dry land. Is it on the water? Use a full sentence.
The house is not on the water.
Two houses stand on dry land. Where are the houses?
The houses are on land.
Sam says, I do not know. You do not know. Agree with Sam.
I do not know either.
Before, both people liked rain, but now Sam does not like rain and you do not like it, so how can you agree with Sam?
I do not like rain either.
Sam says, I do not know. Your answer is the same. Find and fix one word.
I do not know either.
Kim says, I do not know. You do not know. Agree with Kim in a full sentence.
I do not know either.
Kim says, I do not like rain. In the story, you feel the same. Agree with Kim in a full sentence.
I do not like rain either.
Kim says, I do not have a boat. In the story, you have no boat. Agree with Kim in a full sentence.
I do not have a boat either.
The story card shows one house and three bedrooms. Tell me about the bedrooms in one sentence.
The house has three bedrooms.
Now there are two houses with six bedrooms in all. Describe both houses together.
The houses have six bedrooms.
Find and fix one word.
The house has two bathrooms.
The story card shows one house and two bathrooms. Tell me about the bathrooms.
The house has two bathrooms.
The story card shows two houses and two studies in all. Tell me about the studies in both houses.
The houses have two studies.
The story card shows one house and four bedrooms. Tell me about the bedrooms.
The house has four bedrooms.
In this story, you choose the kitchen. Your reason is that you can cook there. Which room do you like, and why?
I like the kitchen because I can cook.
Now two friends choose the living room. Their reason is playing there. Speak for both friends and give their reason.
We like the living room because we can play.
You choose the study. Reading there is your reason. Fix the word that links your choice to your reason.
I like the study because I can read.
In this story, you choose the bedroom. Your reason is that you can rest there. Which room do you like, and why?
I like the bedroom because I can rest.
In this story, your choice is the study for reading, so which room do you like, and why?
I like the study because I can read.
Two friends choose the living room. Their reason is that they can play games there. Speak for both friends. Which room do you like, and why?
We like the living room because we can play games.
In this story, you choose board games for your free time. What do you enjoy?
I enjoy playing board games.
Before, you spoke about yourself. Now Mia likes to read books. Speak about Mia.
She enjoys reading books.
Find and fix one word.
I enjoy playing card games.
In this story, you like to read books. What do you enjoy?
I enjoy reading books.
Two friends like to play card games. Speak for both friends. What do you enjoy?
We enjoy playing card games.
Tom likes to play board games. What does Tom enjoy?
He enjoys playing board games.
Look at the story road. Many cars are moving past. When can it be dangerous?
When there are many cars, it can be dangerous.
Before, the road had many cars. Now there is one fast car. Keep the warning and describe the new scene.
When there is a fast car, it can be dangerous.
Find and fix one word.
When there are many cars, it can be dangerous.
In the story, many cars are moving along the road. When can it be dangerous?
When there are many cars, it can be dangerous.
In the story, one fast car is moving along the road. When can it be dangerous?
When there is a fast car, it can be dangerous.
In the story, many boats are moving close to the houses on the water. When can it be dangerous?
When there are many boats, it can be dangerous.
